paragraphs: Friend, here's the whole song in one breath: David says, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1). Everything after that is David showing what it looks like to have the LORD as your shepherd. His care isn't only on the outside, because He restores David's soul and guides him "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:2-3). FULL. SERVICE. SHEPHERD.

Then the road gets dark, and David doesn't pretend it doesn't. He says, "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). Notice what takes the fear away: the shepherd is with him. I think that's the most honest comfort there is, friend, because it works in the real valleys and not only the pretty meadows.

The song ends with the LORD as a host and as a home. David is at a table "in the presence of my enemies," and his cup overflows (Psalm 23:5). Then he looks at ALL his days: "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). So the big idea is this: with the LORD as your shepherd, you lack nothing, you're never alone in the valley, and you're brought all the way home.
